subject: Design Studio operating-cycle rendering and concurrent design search

environment.webglRenderer: ANGLE (Apple, ANGLE Metal Renderer: Apple M4, Unspecified Version)
environment.launch: Isolated headless browser with channel: chromium; full Chromium, not the default headless shell

method.scenario: Default authored V12 cranktrain, Operating loads panel, engine playback active
method.settling: Camera transition allowed to settle before measurement
method.frameTiming: Consecutive requestAnimationFrame timestamps; p95 is the sorted sample at floor(count * 0.95)
method.longTasks: PerformanceObserver observing longtask entries during each measurement window
method.worker: Real operating-optimization worker: 500 geometry combinations across three prescribed operating conditions, followed by finalist refinement
method.nativeSolverIsolation: The worker reached the first native-analysis request. That request was intercepted with a deliberate QA-only 503 response; no native solve ran during the frame measurements.
method.browserIsolation: Separate browser profile; WebSockets blocked to prevent HMR from resetting the measured page

integratedResults.condition: Operating playback during the real 500-design worker search

interpretation: Approximately 60 Hz frame cadence was maintained in both measured hardware-accelerated windows, including the concurrent design search. The slow default-headless-shell result was specific to software rendering.
limits: Short local measurements on one Apple M4 machine; not a guarantee for other devices, resolutions, browser versions or sustained sessions.
requestAnimationFrame cadence and long-task observations are not GPU timestamp queries, power measurements or an end-to-end input-latency benchmark.
The native meshing/elasticity solve, result adoption, AI requests and thermal throttling were outside these frame measurement windows.
No claim is made that SwiftShader can render this scene at 60 Hz. Its software-rendering result must not be conflated with the hardware Metal measurements.
Frame times are rounded to 0.1 ms. The frame count can include the final interval extending just beyond the requested measurement window.
This record verifies observed rendering behavior; it does not validate the physical assumptions of the operating or structural models.
